page: Amazon Web Services r8idb.2xlarge is an eighth-generation memory-optimized instance managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system is powered by an Intel x86_64 processor operating at 3.9 GHz, featuring 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs with hyperthreading (2 threads per core). It is configured with 64.0 GB of memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio suited for in-memory caching and data-intensive compute operations.

The r8idb.2xlarge includes 474 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a baseline network throughput of 8 Gbps. Unlike diskless alternatives, the local NVMe block storage delivers low-latency disk I/O directly attached to the host server. However, this local instance storage is ephemeral and does not retain data across stop and start cycles, requiring persistence mechanisms to be implemented at the software or cloud volume level. Dedicated GPU hardware is not included.

By combining an 8:1 memory-to-core density with direct-attached NVMe storage, the r8idb.2xlarge provides hardware resource efficiency for workloads that require low-latency scratch space alongside large in-memory datasets. Typical use cases include in-memory key-value databases, distributed caching layers, relational database servers, and real-time transactional analytics engines.
